reply_text:
I read this as **borderline**. The quoted words are on the page exactly, but neither the date nor the prediction is in them. Both come from Fortune's description of the question and the article's framing.

**1. The page.** The Fortune article opened. It is "Top VC Kai-Fu Lee says his prediction that AI will displace 50% of jobs by 2027 is 'uncannily accurate'", by Jason Ma, dated May 25, 2024. The quote is there word for word. The article says he said it at the Fortune Innovation Forum in Hong Kong "in March", on stage with Alyson Shontell. This is a news report, not a transcript, so at best the claim would be coverage only. The article links a YouTube recording of the session (youtube.com/watch?v=zZs447dgMjg). I did not open it.

**2. The four parts of the rule.**
- **Part 1 (role): passes, with a note.** In March 2024 Lee was founder-leader of 01.AI, a company building frontier models, so he held a qualifying role. Fortune calls him only "chairman and chief executive of Sinovation Ventures", so the role comes from his role history, not from the page.
- **Part 2 (looks forward, about AI): weak.** A forecast that AI will displace jobs counts under the rule. But Lee's own words don't state that forecast. They only say an earlier forecast is "uncannily accurate" and "the correct pace". The forecast itself is from 2017, when he was at Sinovation and held no qualifying role. Fortune quotes it: AI "will probably replace 50% of human jobs", and says he "later" put it within 10 years.
- **Part 3 (a date or length of time): fails as written.** Neither 2027 nor "three years" is in his words. It comes from Fortune's paraphrase of the question ("With the timeline of his prediction just three years away, she asked him if it still holds"). We don't have the interviewer's actual wording.
- **Part 4 (primary source): coverage only.** As found, the source is a news report. The linked recording could become a primary source.

**Already recorded?** No. None of his recorded files covers this. The nearest, `2024-03-kaifulee-ai-capabilities-dwarf-humans-two-to-three-years`, is the same month but a different claim.

**For the person checking:** if the recording shows the interviewer saying the 50%-by-2027 timeline and Lee clearly agreeing to it, this could be read as a dated claim from a primary source. Otherwise it stays out and is logged as borderline.
